# Test fixtures

Byte-level fixtures used by wire-compatibility tests. Every fixture must have a
documented provenance so byte-for-byte assertions can be trusted.

## Layout

- `kms/` — KMS REQUEST/RESPONSE v4/v5/v6 golden bytes (Phase 3).
- `crypto/` — AES-CMAC v4 / HMAC-SHA256 v6 vectors (Phase 1).
- `rpc/` — DCE/RPC BIND/REQUEST/RESPONSE frames (Phase 4).
- `kmsdata/` — parsed `.kmd` expectations (Phase 2).

## Data fixture

The canonical KMS data file is `reference/vlmcsd.kmd` (15,079 bytes). Tests load it
at runtime via `std.Io.Dir.readFileAlloc` relative to the build root, to avoid
duplicating the binary (`@embedFile` cannot reference files outside the package
path).

## Provenance

- `reference/vlmcsd.kmd` — original vlmcsd data file, shipped with the C reference.
  Header: magic `"KMD\0"`, version DWORD little-endian (`MajorVer == 2`).
- Protocol/crypto golden bytes — captured from the C reference (one-time
  bootstrap, **outside this repo**) or from a real Windows KMS client capture.

### Crypto vectors (`testdata/crypto/`)

Generated by the one-time bootstrap tool `reference/dump_vectors.c`, which
compiles the C reference crypto implementation (`reference/vlmcsd-src/crypto.c`,
`crypto_internal.c`, `endian.c`) via `reference/Makefile` and prints byte-exact
outputs:

| Fixture | Function (C reference) | Input |
|---------|------------------------|-------|
| `cmac_v4_zeros_32.hex` | `AesCmacV4` | 32 zero bytes |
| `cmac_v4_zeros_16.hex` | `AesCmacV4` | 16 zero bytes |
| `aes_v6_encrypt_zero_block.hex` | `AesInitKey(AesKeyV6, IsV6=1)` + `AesEncryptBlock` | zero block |
| `aes_v5_encrypt_zero_block.hex` | `AesInitKey(AesKeyV5, IsV6=0)` + `AesEncryptBlock` | zero block |
| `aes_v6_decrypt_zero_block.hex` | `AesInitKey(AesKeyV6, IsV6=1)` + `AesDecryptBlock` | ciphertext of zero block |
| `aes_cbc_encrypt_zeros32_v6.hex` | `AesEncryptCbc` (v6 key, zero IV) | 32 zero bytes (PKCS#7-padded to 48) |
| `aes_cbc_decrypt_zeros32_v6.hex` | `AesDecryptCbc` (v6 key, zero IV) | 48 ciphertext bytes |
| `hmac_sha256_zeros_32.hex` | `Sha256Hmac` (16-byte key hardcoded) | zero key, 32 zero bytes |

## Generating a fixture from captured bytes

Once reference bytes are captured, turn them into a committed hex fixture:

- Programmatic (inside tests/tools): `src/testutil.zig` `hexDump` returns a
  lowercase hex string of a byte slice.
- One-off manual dump (bootstrap only):
  `xxd -p -c 256 <binary> > testdata/<name>.hex`

Record the source command/tool and date next to each fixture in this file so the
provenance stays auditable.
